question: Kajari is a folk song and dance genre of India. It has its roots in ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __Uttar Pradesh.__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• Kajri Folk Song is related to Uttar Pradesh __as well as Bihar.
 
• Kajri folk song is often used to describe the longing of a maiden for her lover as the black monsoon cloud arrives in the summer skies, and the style is notably sung during the rainy season.
 
• Kajri folk song is traditionally sung in the villages and towns of Uttar Pradesh around Banaras, Mirzapur, Mathura, Allahabad, and the Bhojpur regions of Bihar.
 
• Maand Folk Song is the traditional folk song of Rajasthan whereas Koli and Lavani Folk Songs belong to Maharashtra and Himachal Pradesh is enriched with the great folk song Jhoori.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Kerala is known for its traditional dance forms such as Kathakali and Mohiniyattam, which are quite different from Kajari.
 
• West Bengal has a rich tradition of folk music and dance forms, including Baul, Jhumur, and Chhau, but Kajari is not one of them.
 
• Punjab is known for its energetic and vibrant Bhangra dance form, which is quite different from the graceful and melodious Kajari.
 
• Uttar Pradesh is the correct answer as Kajari has its roots in this state and is still widely performed here.
